EFTA01034254

 Does U.S. recognition of Israeli sovereignty over the
Golan Heights violate UN Resolution 242?
Opponents of President Donald Trump's decision
to recognize Israeli sovereignty over the Golan
Heights have argued it violates UN Resolution
242. That resolution long ago lost its relevance
and it is only trotted out when convenient to
criticize Israel. Having already annexed the
Golan, the issue was already moot. Resolution
242 does not preclude Israel from annexing the
Golan Heights. U.S. recognition acknowledges this fact.

"Misreading Polls on Israel —Again"
by Mitchell Bard
Gallup has released its annual survey on American public opinion
toward Israel, and the reactions were predictably a mixture of hysteria
and misinformation.
Typical was this Haaretz headline — "New Poll Shows Support for
Israel Plummeting Among U.S. Liberals, Millennials and Women" —
and this one from The Times of Israel: "New poll: Americans' support
for Israel falls to lowest point in a decade."
Was the data really that dire?

American Public Opinion Toward

Support for Israel is not restricted to the
Jewish community. Americans of all ages,
races and religions sympathize with Israel.
This support is also nonpartisan.
The organization that has conducted the most
surveys is Gallup. In the most recent poll,
reported by Gallup in February 2019, 59% of
Americans sympathized with Israel.
